claims.text: A Service with no type field gets type ClusterIP: an address reachable only from inside the cluster (output shows TYPE ClusterIP, EXTERNAL-IP <none>).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services, Load Balancing, and Networking > Service (Service type: ClusterIP is the default); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/ingress.txt lines 1-3

claims.text: An Ingress exposes HTTP(S) routes from outside the cluster to Services; each rule has an optional host and a list of paths, each path with a backend of service.name and service.port.number (or name).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services, Load Balancing, and Networking > Ingress (What is Ingress?; Ingress rules)

claims.text: Both the host and the path of a rule must match the incoming request before traffic is sent to the rule's Service; the host is compared with the request's Host header, which an HTTP client such as curl fills from the host (and port) of the URL.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > Ingress rules ('Both the host and path must match'); Name based virtual hosting; RFC 9110 §7.2 Host (client sets Host from the target URI authority)

claims.text: Every Ingress path needs a pathType; Prefix matches element-wise on the path split by '/' (so /api/v1 matches /api/v1/products but not /api/v1x); Exact matches the URL path exactly.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > Path types; Examples table (/aaa/bbb vs /aaa/bbbxyz: no match)

claims.text: Only creating an Ingress resource has no effect; an Ingress controller must run to satisfy it, and Ingress controllers are not started automatically with a cluster (unlike controllers in kube-controller-manager).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > Prerequisites; Concepts > Ingress Controllers (opening paragraph)

claims.text: Traefik's Kubernetes Ingress provider watches Ingress objects through the Kubernetes API and builds its routing from their rules.
claims.source_hint: Traefik docs: Providers > Kubernetes Ingress (the provider watches the API server for Ingress resources); scripts/k8s/ingress.sh lines 24-25 comment

claims.text: When no router matches a request, Traefik itself answers 404; at stage-3 the call before the Ingress exists prints HTTP 404 and the call after prints HTTP 200 with the products.
claims.source_hint: Traefik docs: Routing > Routers (no matching router → 404 Not Found); scripts/k8s/ingress.sh lines 18-19; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/ingress.txt lines 5-6, 14-16

claims.text: ingressClassName names the Ingress's class, the name under which a controller takes it; on donhang-staging Traefik acts on an Ingress of class traefik (output CLASS traefik, then 200); an Ingress naming another class is left to another controller.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > IngressClass; Traefik docs: Kubernetes Ingress provider (ingressClass); ingress.txt lines 10-12

claims.text: Ingress controllers use annotations to configure behaviour beyond the Ingress spec; which annotations are expected or supported depends on each controller, and controllers operate slightly differently.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > The Ingress resource ('Ingress controllers frequently use annotations… Review the documentation for your choice of ingress controller'); Ingress > Prerequisites

claims.text: Annotations are arbitrary key-value metadata on an object, stored in metadata.annotations.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Working with Kubernetes Objects > Annotations

claims.text: A controller may ignore an annotation it does not define or interpret a same-named one differently, so an Ingress moved between controllers usually keeps its routing but can lose annotation-driven behaviour.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > Prerequisites ('the various Ingress controllers operate slightly differently') and The Ingress resource (annotations per controller)

claims.text: api-ingress.yaml: ingressClassName traefik (line 11), one rule lines 12-22: host ingress.donhang.localhost, path /api/v1, pathType Prefix, backend Service api port 8080; it is a lesson manifest under deploy/k8s/lessons, not in deploy/gitops/config-repo.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/k8s/lessons/api-ingress.yaml lines 1-22 at stage-3; outline depth_notes

claims.text: When ingress.sh ran at stage-3, curl reached Traefik on this machine at ingress.donhang.localhost:18080 with no DNS entry for that name anywhere in the repository.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/ingress.txt lines 14-16

claims.text: ingress.sh: url and status() at lines 8-9 (status prints only the code), show() at line 6 prints '$ <command>' then runs it; after apply it polls once a second up to 60 times for 200 (line 29), prints the body cut to 120 characters (line 32) and deletes the Ingress (line 37).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang scripts/k8s/ingress.sh lines 8-9, 26-37 at stage-3

claims.text: Traefik applies a newly stored Ingress shortly after the API server stores it, not synchronously with kubectl apply (hence the script's wait loop).
claims.source_hint: Traefik docs: Providers > Kubernetes Ingress (watch-based, throttleDuration); scripts/k8s/ingress.sh line 29

claims.text: apps/traefik.yaml sets Traefik's Service type NodePort, nodePort 30080 (web); main.tf maps node port 30080 to host port 18080. A NodePort Service opens that port on every node and forwards what arrives there to the Service's Pods.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/gitops/config-repo/apps/traefik.yaml lines 30-37, deploy/tofu/envs/staging/cluster/main.tf lines 18-21 at stage-3; kubernetes.io: Service > type: NodePort

claims.text: On a cloud provider that supports external load balancers, a Service of type LoadBalancer has the cloud provision an external load balancer: an outside IP address whose traffic is passed to the Service.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Service > type: LoadBalancer

claims.text: An Ingress backend refers to a Service by name and port; Traefik uses that Service to find the Pods and sends each request to one of them (nativeLBByDefault false), so the Ingress does not replace the Service.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > Ingress rules (backend = Service and port names); Traefik docs: Kubernetes Ingress provider (nativeLBByDefault)

claims.text: kubectl apply of an Ingress prints 'created' whether or not any controller acts on it; kubectl get ingress lists it either way. -o custom-columns replaces kubectl get's default columns with the ones named.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > Prerequisites; kubectl reference: Output options (custom-columns); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/ingress.txt line 9

claims.text: The basic Ingress rules (host, path, pathType, backend) are fields of the Ingress spec defined by Kubernetes itself, so any Ingress controller reads them; controllers may still operate slightly differently.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Ingress > The Ingress resource; Ingress rules; Prerequisites ('the various Ingress controllers operate slightly differently')
